description: We are a multidisciplinary team of developers and researchers who believe that the best way to understand the cosmos is to step directly into the mission control seat. Combining technical craftsmanship in Unity and C#, we set out to bridge the gap between complex aerospace science and engaging, accessible gameplay. Just like a real lunar mission, MOONIES was brought to life by a dedicated crew united by a shared passion for space exploration, interactive storytelling and science education.
summary:
MONNIES is an educational 2D space adventure built in Unity for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Barcelona. Created to help people understand the challenges astronauts face in space while operating a spacecraft, it makes every decision matter. Players choose a crew character (Commander, Pilot, Engineer or Medic), explore a three-deck spacecraft and keep its systems running on a roughly 10-minute flight from Earth orbit to the Moon and back.
Randomized missions and emergencies, inspired by NASA’s Artemis II, include solar radiation storms, docking problems, cabin pressure leaks and system failures. Players operate onboard equipment, manage everything on board, complete every assigned task and try to survive the flight. Mission Control messages, chosen by a weighted randomizer, guide them and add real mission context.
Moonies turns mission design into hands-on decision-making and shows how crews, systems and operations work together on a lunar mission. It matters because it brings the excitement of Artemis to young players in an accessible, replayable way, building decision-making skills and curiosity about space to inspire the next generation of explorers.
details:
This project is an educational simulation game designed to teach people about the real challenges astronauts face during space missions. Players can choose from four different crew roles: commander, engineer, medic, or pilot. Their main mission is to safely navigate the spacecraft to the Moon. Along the way, players must handle unexpected emergencies and manage ship operations under pressure until the entire crew reaches their destination.

The main benefit of the game is that it teaches through hands-on experience. Instead of simply reading about space travel, players feel the stress, responsibility, and quick decision-making required to operate a spacecraft. Our team built the project using the Unity game engine, writing scripts in C# with the assistance of AI tools + Unity. Ultimately, our goal was to give players a realistic sense of what it truly means to be an astronaut and how difficult it is to operate a spacecraft during a real mission.

In 2026, NASA celebrates a monumental dual triumph: 50 years since the historic Viking landers first touched down on the Red Planet and revealed its secrets to the world, and the bold shattering of a half-century barrier as Artemis II sends astronauts back around the Moon for the first time since the Apollo era!

Driven by this spirit, we created MOONIES—a heartfelt tribute to the brilliant minds and dedicated professionals whose tireless work turns humanity's greatest space milestones into reality. From this very first launch, we hope MOONIES ignites your curiosity and inspires a new generation of explorers to reach for the stars and push the boundaries of space even further.
